title: Implantable sensors in modern healthcare: advances, clinical applications, and future directions
content: Implantable sensors are emerging as powerful tools for continuous, real-time monitoring of physiological and biochemical parameters, thus facilitating improved disease diagnosis, therapeutic monitoring, and personalized healthcare. Recent advances in microelectronics, materials science, and wireless technologies have accelerated the development of miniaturized implantable devices with enhanced sensitivity, biocompatibility, and long-term operational stability. This review outlines the fundamental principles and major categories of implantable sensors, including biochemical, electrophysiological, pressure, and temperature sensing systems. Particular attention is given to material selection, biointerface engineering, wireless communication, data processing, and integration with biological environments. Current applications in chronic disease management, cardiovascular monitoring, neuroengineering, and precision medicine are highlighted alongside key challenges related to biofouling, immune responses, power supply, device reliability, and data security. Ethical, regulatory, and clinical translation considerations are also examined. Finally, emerging trends in smart materials, self-powered platforms, and intelligent implantable systems are discussed, emphasizing their potential to advance next-generation healthcare technologies.
